topic: What is an LLM, explained simply

slides.headline: An AI that writes essays is just *guessing* words.
subtitle: What an LLM is, in plain words, with examples.
No maths needed.
slides.narration: Let's understand and learn LLM in one minute. Have you seen a chatbot write an email? Here is how it works.

slides.heading: What an LLM *is*
body: A program that read huge amounts of text, then learned how words fit together.
slides.narration: LLM stands for Large Language Model. It learns from huge amounts of text, like books and websites.

slides.heading: It predicts the *next word*
body: You type: "The cat sat on the"
It guesses the likeliest next word: "mat".
slides.narration: It predicts the next word. You type the cat sat on the, and it picks mat.

slides.heading: Why it is called *large*
body: Its connections number in the billions.
Together they hold patterns of grammar, facts and style.
slides.narration: It is large because it has billions of connections. Each one acts as one of many tiny dials, tuned while it learns.

slides.heading: Examples you already *use*
body: Chatbots that answer your questions in plain English.
Autocomplete in email, and code helpers that suggest the next line.
slides.narration: You already use it in a chatbot and in email autocomplete. Same idea, different job.

slides.heading: What it is *not*
body: It is not a search engine checking live facts.
It can sound sure and still be wrong, so verify.
slides.narration: It is not a search engine. It can sound sure and still be wrong.

slides.headline: It sounds like thinking, but it is predicting.
slides.cta: Follow vivektraces for the next one.
slides.narration: So an LLM predicts words, again and again. That is why it sounds like thinking. Follow vivektraces for the next one.
